emtech_AAU_2024.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AAU_2024.text: 1. Nanotechnologies are best known for enlarging things. (2024)
emtech_AAU_2024.explanation: Nanotechnology involves the manipulation of matter on an atomic and molecular scale, typically between 1 and 100 nanometers. It is best known for miniaturizing systems and devices, not enlarging them.

emtech_AAU_2024.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AAU_2024.text: 2. Narrow AI is the most common type of AI that performs a dedicated task with [truncated] (2024)
emtech_AAU_2024.explanation: Narrow AI, or Weak AI, is designed and trained to perform a dedicated, specific task with high proficiency, such as facial recognition or language translation. It is the only type of AI that currently exists in practical applications, making it the most common.

emtech_AAU_2024.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AAU_2024.text: 3. Interoperability challenge is not an issue in the Internet of things. (2024)
emtech_AAU_2024.explanation: Interoperability is a major challenge in the Internet of Things due to the vast variety of heterogeneous devices, protocols, and platforms. Achieving seamless communication across these diverse systems remains a critical issue for scalable IoT deployments.

emtech_AAU_2024.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AAU_2024.text: 4. Augmented reality enables to superficially interact with the environment in r[truncated] (2024)
emtech_AAU_2024.explanation: Augmented Reality enables users to deeply and meaningfully interact with integrated physical and virtual environments in real-time. This interaction is spatial and highly interactive, contrasting with a purely 'superficial' overlay.

emtech_AAU_2024.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AAU_2024.text: 5. Video see-through device uses an HMD (head-mounted-device) that employ[truncated] merge the images within an open-view HMD. (2024)
emtech_AAU_2024.explanation: Video see-through systems use closed-view head-mounted displays equipped with cameras that capture the real world and blend it with virtual elements on a screen. In contrast, optical see-through systems use an open-view transparent display.

emtech_AAU_2024.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AAU_2024.text: 6. Today many insurance companies are installing black boxes in customer car[truncated] behavior and adjusting premiums accordingly. (2024)
emtech_AAU_2024.explanation: Usage-based insurance heavily relies on telematics 'black boxes' installed in vehicles to monitor driving behavior. This IoT application allows insurance companies to dynamically adjust premiums based on real-world risk metrics like speed and braking.

emtech_AAU_2024.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AAU_2024.text: 7. Information security is broader than cyber security in that it protects inform[truncated] representation as well. (2024)
emtech_AAU_2024.explanation: Information security broadly encompasses the protection of all forms of information, whether digital, physical, or verbal. Cybersecurity is a specialized subset focused strictly on defending digital assets, electronic systems, and networks.

emtech_AAU_2024.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AAU_2024.text: 8. Ambient Intelligence poses a serious privacy concern. (2024)
emtech_AAU_2024.explanation: Ambient Intelligence relies on ubiquitous computing and pervasive environmental sensing to track and respond to human presence. This constant, invisible data collection and continuous surveillance inherently raise severe privacy and data security concerns.

emtech_AAU_2024.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AAU_2024.text: 9. Vulnerability is the protection of computer systems from theft of or d[truncated] software, or electronic data. (2024)
emtech_AAU_2024.explanation: Cybersecurity is the discipline dedicated to protecting computer systems from the theft of or damage to their hardware, software, or electronic data. A vulnerability, on the other hand, is a specific weakness or flaw within a system that can be exploited by threats.

emtech_AAU_2024.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AAU_2024.text: 10. The Internet boom has provided many benefits for society and Intern[truncated] negative aspects. (2024)
emtech_AAU_2024.explanation: While the Internet boom has revolutionized global communication, education, and business, delivering massive societal benefits, it has simultaneously introduced significant negative aspects such as cybercrime, privacy erosion, and the rapid spread of misinformation.

emtech_AAU_2024.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AAU_2024.text: 1. Brewing and baking bread are examples of processes that fall within the c[truncated] (2024)
emtech_AAU_2024.explanation: Biotechnology uses living organisms or their biological systems to produce useful products. Traditional processes like brewing beer and baking bread utilize yeast fermentation, making them fundamental examples of biotechnology.

emtech_AAU_2024.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AAU_2024.text: 2. Of the following is NOT among the technological enablers of IoT. (2024)

options.text: C. Nano technology used for shrinking things
D. smart technology used for thinking the things

emtech_AAU_2024.explanation: Core technological enablers of IoT include RFID, wireless sensor networks, nanotechnology, and smart processing technologies that allow devices to perceive and communicate. While SSL is an important protocol for protecting data in transit, it is an IT security safeguard rather than a foundational technology that physically enables IoT device connectivity.

emtech_AAU_2024.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AAU_2024.text: 3. All of the following belong to types of IoT systems except______ (2024)
emtech_AAU_2024.explanation: Wearable devices, smartphones, and wireless sensor networks are fundamental types of connected IoT systems. Legacy systems refer to outdated, traditional computing hardware that inherently lacks IoT connectivity and network capabilities.

emtech_AAU_2024.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AAU_2024.text: 4. All of the following are IoT cloud development platforms except (2024)
emtech_AAU_2024.explanation: Microsoft Azure (often misspelled as Assure), Salesforce, and IBM Watson are highly prominent cloud development platforms that provide extensive IoT management and analytics services. The truncated option starting with 'Tec' does not correspond to a major, recognized IoT cloud platform.

emtech_AAU_2024.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AAU_2024.text: 5. Which of the following is not the advantage of IoT? (2024)

options.text: B. IoT provides real-world information leading to the more effective management of resources
D. If there's a bug in the system, it's likely that every connected device will become corrupted.

emtech_AAU_2024.explanation: A massive, interconnected network of devices inherently expands the attack surface, meaning a single bug or vulnerability could potentially propagate and corrupt the entire network. This represents a critical disadvantage of IoT, whereas improved engagement and resource management are core benefits.

emtech_AAU_2024.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AAU_2024.text: 6. Which layer of the IoT architecture is responsible to take measurements such as temperature, air quality, speed, humidity, pressure, flow, movement and electricity etc.? (2024)
emtech_AAU_2024.explanation: The Perception Layer, also known as the Smart Devices Layer, sits at the bottom of the IoT architecture. It utilizes physical sensors and actuators to continuously gather environmental measurements like temperature, humidity, and movement to pass up to higher layers.

emtech_AAU_2024.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AAU_2024.text: 7. Which of the following is wrong about IoT? (2024)

options.text: A. It is about intelligent network of devices which are capable of sensing, accumulating and transferring data autonomously and automatically.
B. There are fewer number of IoT devices today than the size of the global human population.
C. Network of smart objects with inherent constraints such as power, bandwidth, storage etc.
D. Machine to machine (M2M) offers the connectivity that enables IoT.

emtech_AAU_2024.explanation: The global number of connected IoT devices surpassed the human population several years ago and currently numbers in the tens of billions. Therefore, the assertion that there are fewer IoT devices than humans is factually incorrect.

emtech_AAU_2024.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AAU_2024.text: 8. Of the multi-tier augmented reality (AR) system architecture ___________________ is concerned about managing process workflows, access controls, and fetching and storing data. (2024)
emtech_AAU_2024.explanation: In a standard multi-tier Augmented Reality architecture, the AR System Server functions as the core backend logic handler. It is directly responsible for managing process workflows, enforcing access controls, and coordinating the fetching and storing of data between the client applications and the database tier.

emtech_AAU_2024.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AAU_2024.text: 9. In which type of reality can you interact with and manipulate both physical and virtual items and environments, using next-generation sensing and imaging technologies? (2024)
emtech_AAU_2024.explanation: Mixed Reality (MR) seamlessly merges real and virtual worlds to produce new environments where physical and digital objects dynamically co-exist. Unlike standard Augmented Reality, which typically acts as an overlay, MR allows users to physically interact with and manipulate both real-world and digital items.

emtech_AAU_2024.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AAU_2024.text: 10. Of the components in an AR system architecture ___________ is responsible for proper alignment of the real and virtual objects. (2024)
emtech_AAU_2024.explanation: The tracking system within an AR architecture continuously calculates the user's position and orientation in real physical space. This precise pose tracking is strictly required to ensure that virtual objects remain properly anchored, registered, and aligned with the physical environment as the user's perspective changes.

emtech_AAU_2024.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AAU_2024.text: 11. Which of the following is a not characteristic of Augmented Reality? (2024)

options.text: B. Visual contact with the physical world

emtech_AAU_2024.explanation: Augmented Reality is classically defined by its ability to combine real and virtual worlds, be interactive in real-time, and perfectly register virtual objects in 3D physical space. Since AR annotations can frequently consist of flat, 2D text or graphics mapped to the environment, a strictly '3D-Display of Virtual Object' is not a mandatory characteristic.

emtech_AAU_2024.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AAU_2024.text: 15. One of the following cannot be considered as General Ethical Principles (2024)
emtech_AAU_2024.explanation: Fundamental ethical principles in computing and technology include actively avoiding harm, respecting user privacy, and honoring data confidentiality. Bias is a harmful prejudice or systematic flaw in algorithms and decision-making that professionals actively seek to eliminate, making it unethical rather than a guiding principle.

emtech_AAU_2024.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AAU_2024.text: 16. One of the following cybersecurity threats is designed to extort money by blocking access to computer files or systems. (2024)
emtech_AAU_2024.explanation: Ransomware is a highly specific category of malicious software that encrypts a victim's files or entirely locks them out of their system. The attacker then extorts the victim by demanding a financial payment (a ransom) to restore access to the compromised data.

emtech_AAU_2024.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AAU_2024.text: 17. One of the following types of computer vision is used to determine the identity of individuals in an image. (2024)
emtech_AAU_2024.explanation: Facial recognition is a specialized computer vision technology engineered to identify or verify a person's identity by mapping and analyzing complex facial features from digital imagery. It is distinct from broader methods like edge or object detection, which do not inherently seek to determine human identity.

emtech_AAU_2024.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AAU_2024.text: 18. Which digital privacy principle dictates to collect the minimal amount of information necessary from individuals and businesses consistent with the organization's mission and legal requirements? (2024)
emtech_AAU_2024.explanation: Data minimization is a foundational privacy principle, heavily emphasized in frameworks like the GDPR, which dictates that organizations must only collect the absolute minimum personal data necessary to achieve their specific legal or business objectives. This practice mitigates risk and protects user privacy.

emtech_AAU_2024.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AAU_2024.text: 19. One of the following is not a part of embedded system advantages (2024)
emtech_AAU_2024.explanation: Developing embedded systems typically requires a high development effort due to the complex constraints of hardware-software co-design, strict timing requirements, and heavily limited memory. This complexity represents a significant disadvantage, unlike the benefits of low cost and customized enhanced performance.

emtech_AAU_2024.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AAU_2024.text: 20. One of the following type of data forms is known to be important in big data systems for performing preliminary analytics (2024)
emtech_AAU_2024.explanation: Metadata, which represents 'data about data,' provides essential descriptive context such as file source, format, and creation date. In large-scale big data systems, metadata allows analysts to perform rapid preliminary analytics and categorize information without incurring the heavy computational cost of processing the full underlying dataset.

emtech_HU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_HU_2021.text: 1. IOT devices do most of the work without human intervention, Although people can interact with the devices (2021)
emtech_HU_2021.explanation: Internet of Things (IoT) devices are designed to operate primarily through machine-to-machine communication and automated processes. While they function largely without human intervention, user interfaces and control mechanisms allow humans to interact with them when necessary.

emtech_HU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_HU_2021.text: 2. The key characteristic of virtual reality is begin able to create a real time interaction between contents in real word with that of the synthetic content. (2021)
emtech_HU_2021.explanation: The characteristic described—interacting with both real-world and synthetic (virtual) content simultaneously in real time—defines Augmented Reality (AR) or Mixed Reality (MR). Virtual Reality (VR), by contrast, completely immerses the user in a fully synthetic environment, replacing the real world.

emtech_HU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_HU_2021.text: 3. Augmented reality is a form of Emerging Technologies that allows users to overlay computer generated content in the real world. (2021)
emtech_HU_2021.explanation: Augmented Reality (AR) enhances the physical world by overlaying digital elements (such as visual, auditory, or sensory information) onto the real-world environment, allowing users to perceive both simultaneously.

emtech_HU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_HU_2021.text: 4. Artificial intelligence is a new word and a new technology for researchers. (2021)
emtech_HU_2021.explanation: Artificial Intelligence is not a new term or a newly discovered technology. The field was officially established as an academic discipline at the Dartmouth Conference in 1956, meaning it has been an active area of research for many decades.

emtech_HU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_HU_2021.text: 5. The first intelligent humanoid robot was built in FORTAN. (2021)
emtech_HU_2021.explanation: The statement contains a factual and conceptual error. The first full-scale intelligent humanoid robot, WABOT-1, was built at Waseda University in Japan in 1973. 'FORTRAN' is an early high-level programming language, not a place or a robotic platform, making the assertion false.

emtech_HU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_HU_2021.text: 1. The augmented reality system (ARS) which mixed the virtual content with the real content and sent the result to video out module is _______? (2021)
emtech_HU_2021.explanation: In an Augmented Reality System (ARS), the visual unit is responsible for taking the virtual, computer-generated content and seamlessly mixing it with the live feed of the real world before sending the combined output to the display module.

emtech_HU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_HU_2021.text: 2. One of the following is not advantage of artificial intelligence. (2021)
emtech_HU_2021.explanation: None of the listed options (AI itself, Cloud computing, or Big data) are 'advantages' of Artificial Intelligence. They are related technological fields and paradigms. Therefore, 'All of the above' correctly identifies that none represent an advantage of AI.

emtech_HU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_HU_2021.text: 3. ______ is a multi-disciplinary field that uses scientific methods, processes, algorithms, and systems to extract knowledge. (2021)
emtech_HU_2021.explanation: Data science is the multidisciplinary field that relies on scientific methods, algorithms, data mining techniques, and systems to extract valuable insights and structured knowledge from raw, noisy, and unstructured data.

emtech_HU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_HU_2021.text: 4. ______ can be defined as a representation of facts, concepts, or instructions in a formalized manner (2021)
emtech_HU_2021.explanation: Data is formally defined as raw facts, concepts, or instructions represented in a formalized, structured manner suitable for communication, interpretation, or processing by human or machine. Information is data that has been processed to have meaning.

emtech_HU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_HU_2021.text: 5. ______ is a term generally used to describe a new technology. (2021)
emtech_HU_2021.explanation: The term 'Emerging Technologies' specifically describes newly developed or currently developing technologies that are expected to significantly alter the business and social environment, such as AI, IoT, and blockchain.

emtech_HU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_HU_2021.text: 6. ______ is a form of Emerging Technologies that allows users to overlay computer-generated content in the real world (2021)
emtech_HU_2021.explanation: Augmented Reality (AR) specifically refers to the technology that superimposes computer-generated images, data, or sound onto a user's view of the real world, enhancing their current perception of reality.

emtech_HU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_HU_2021.text: 7. ______ machines will be super intelligent and will have their own consciousness, sentiments, and self-wariness. (2021)
emtech_HU_2021.explanation: Self-Aware AI refers to the theoretical future stage of artificial intelligence where machines possess true consciousness, self-awareness, and emotions, surpassing simple understanding to achieve sentience.

emtech_HU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_HU_2021.text: 8. The first AI winter (2021)
emtech_HU_2021.explanation: The first 'AI Winter,' a period characterized by reduced funding and interest in artificial intelligence research due to unfulfilled promises and high expectations, occurred primarily between 1974 and 1980.

emtech_HU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_HU_2021.text: 9. Digital Assistant AI can be very useful to provide digital assistant to users such as AI technology ______ is currently used by various E-commerce websites to show the products as per customer requirements. (2021)
emtech_HU_2021.explanation: It is true that AI-driven digital assistants and recommendation algorithms are extensively utilized across E-commerce websites to personalize the shopping experience and display products tailored to specific customer needs and behaviors.

emtech_HU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_HU_2021.text: 10. which one of the following is not an application of iot ? (2021)
emtech_HU_2021.explanation: Smart devices, smart agriculture, connected cars, and home automation are all primary and prominent applications of the Internet of Things (IoT). Therefore, 'none' of the listed options is NOT an application.

emtech_HU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_HU_2021.text: 11. Allowing medical surgery to look at patient while they see an overly an example of ______ (2021)
emtech_HU_2021.explanation: In medicine, projecting data, MRI scans, or vital statistics as an overlay onto a patient's body while a surgeon operates is a classic application of Augmented Reality (AR). It provides essential data without forcing the surgeon to look away from the real world.

emtech_HU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_HU_2021.text: 12. The interne of thing operates at ______ scale (2021)
emtech_HU_2021.explanation: The Internet of Things fundamentally shifts computing from a human scale to a machine scale. It is characterized by massive Machine-to-Machine (M2M) communication networks where automated devices communicate without necessary human interaction.

emtech_HU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_HU_2021.text: 13. Which one of the following is true advantage of AR? (2021)
emtech_HU_2021.explanation: None of the provided options (Cloud computing, hybrid reality, High-speed) serve as a direct functional advantage of Augmented Reality itself. They are either separate technologies, synonyms (hybrid reality), or generic attributes.

emtech_HU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_HU_2021.text: 14. ______ Requires innovative forms of information processing to draw insights, automate processes, and help decision making. (2021)
emtech_HU_2021.explanation: According to the widely accepted Gartner definition, Big Data requires cost-effective, innovative forms of information processing for enhanced insight discovery, automation, and decision-making.

emtech_HU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_HU_2021.text: 15. Which one of the following main purpose of the sensing layer is to identify any phenomena in the devices' peripheral and obtain data from the real world? (2021)
emtech_HU_2021.explanation: The question essentially defines the Sensing (or Perception) Layer of an IoT architecture, whose core function is to detect phenomena in the environment, collect raw data via sensors, and convert it into digital signals.

emtech_HU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_HU_2021.text:
Part III: Matching the following items (2 points)

"A"
1. Virtual reality
2. Aquaculture fisheries
3. Mixed reality
4. Compliance
5. High-speed

"B"
A. To breed via gonadotropin-releasing hormone
B. advantage of artificial intelligence
C. challenge of iot
D. computer-simulated
E. hybrid reality
F. virtual content aligned (2021)
emtech_HU_2021.explanation: Virtual reality maps to 'computer-simulated' (D) as it generates fully artificial environments. Aquaculture fisheries utilize IoT/biotech such as breeding via gonadotropin-releasing hormone (A). Mixed reality is synonymously referred to as 'hybrid reality' (E). Compliance regarding data privacy and regulations is a major 'challenge of IoT' (C). Finally, 'high-speed' data processing is a core 'advantage of artificial intelligence' (B).

emtech_HU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_HU_2021.text: 1. ______________ acts as a communication channel to transfer data, collected in the sensing layer, to other connected devices. (2021)
emtech_HU_2021.explanation: In an IoT architecture, the network layer (also called the transmission layer) is responsible for routing and transmitting data gathered by the sensing layer securely to different devices or cloud-based processing platforms.

emtech_HU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_HU_2021.text: 2. ______________ understand human emotions, people, beliefs, and be able to interact socially like humans. (2021)
emtech_HU_2021.explanation: Theory of Mind AI is a highly advanced, currently theoretical class of artificial intelligence designed to comprehend that people and objects have thoughts, feelings, and beliefs that affect their behavior, allowing the AI to interact socially.

emtech_HU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_HU_2021.text: 3. ______________ "man-made," and intelligence defines "thinking power", or "the ability to learn and solve problems" hence Artificial Intelligence means "a man-made thinking power." (2021)
emtech_HU_2021.explanation: The breakdown of the term 'Artificial Intelligence' stems from its two root words: 'Artificial' meaning man-made or synthetic, and 'Intelligence' referring to cognitive power and the capacity to solve problems.

emtech_HU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_HU_2021.text: 4. Artificial Intelligence can be divided into various types, there are ______________ and ______________ (2021)
emtech_HU_2021.explanation: At a high level, Artificial Intelligence is predominantly categorized into Narrow AI (or Weak AI), which is designed to perform specific tasks, and General AI (or Strong AI), which possesses generalized human cognitive abilities.

emtech_HU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_HU_2021.text: 5. ______________ AI is a type of AI which is able to perform a dedicated task with intelligence. (2021)
emtech_HU_2021.explanation: Narrow AI (also known as Weak AI) is tailored and trained to perform a single specific or dedicated task, such as facial recognition, internet searches, or driving a car, without broader consciousness or intelligence.

emtech_HU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_HU_2021.text: 1. Explain IoT stack? (2021)
emtech_HU_2021.answer: The IoT stack is a multi-layered technological architecture that defines how an IoT system operates. It generally comprises the Device/Perception Layer (hardware and sensors), the Network/Connectivity Layer (communication protocols and gateways), the Data Processing/Edge Layer (for analyzing and filtering data), and the Application Layer (user interface and business logic).
emtech_HU_2021.explanation: A complete answer must identify that the IoT stack is an architectural framework and list its primary functional layers, which move from raw hardware data collection all the way up to user-facing applications and analytics.

emtech_HU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_HU_2021.text: 2. What is Connectivity? (2021)
emtech_HU_2021.answer: Connectivity in IoT refers to the networking infrastructure, communication protocols, and wireless technologies (such as Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, 5G, or LoRaWAN) that enable IoT devices to communicate, exchange data with one another, and connect to cloud platforms or central servers.
emtech_HU_2021.explanation: Connectivity is the critical link in an IoT ecosystem. Without a communication medium to transmit sensor data to processing hubs, devices remain isolated and non-functional within an IoT context.

emtech_HU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_HU_2021.text: 3. What are the main parts of the IoT system? (2021)
emtech_HU_2021.answer: The main parts of an IoT system include sensors/devices (for physical data collection), connectivity (networks and protocols for data transmission), data processing (cloud or edge computing for data analysis), and a user interface (for human interaction, visualization, and control).
emtech_HU_2021.explanation: An IoT system is holistic, requiring hardware to gather data, a network to move it, processing power to make sense of it, and a UI to make the resulting insights actionable for users.

emtech_HU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_HU_2021.text: 4. List out at list top five currently available emerged technologies? (2021)
emtech_HU_2021.answer:
1. Artificial Intelligence (AI)
2. Internet of Things (IoT)
3. Blockchain Technology
4. Cloud Computing
5. Augmented Reality (AR) and Virtual Reality (VR)
emtech_HU_2021.explanation: These technologies represent the core pillars of the Fourth Industrial Revolution, fundamentally altering computational power, data tracking, immersive experiences, and machine-to-machine automation across modern industries.

emtech_HU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_HU_2021.text: 5. Define artificial intelligence? (2021)
emtech_HU_2021.answer: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is a branch of Emerging Technologies focused on creating systems capable of performing tasks that typically require human intelligence. This involves capabilities such as learning from data, reasoning, problem-solving, understanding natural language, and autonomous decision-making.
emtech_HU_2021.explanation: A robust definition of AI focuses both on its origin (a subset of Emerging Technologies) and its goal (simulating human cognitive processes computationally to solve complex problems).

emtech_SCI_2013.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_SCI_2013.text: 1. Expert systems can exhibit intelligent behavior with the capability to learn, Demonstrate, explain and advice its users. (2013)
emtech_SCI_2013.explanation: Expert systems are a branch of Artificial Intelligence designed to solve complex problems within a specific domain by simulating the judgment and behavior of a human expert. They are built to reason through bodies of knowledge to demonstrate intelligent behavior, explain their logical processes, and provide informed advice to users.

emtech_SCI_2013.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_SCI_2013.text: 2. Chat-bots and robo-advisors are examples of rule-based Systems. (2013)
emtech_SCI_2013.explanation: In fundamental AI architectures, many classical chat-bots and robo-advisors operate on rule-based systems (using 'if-then' logic structures) to parse user inputs and provide structured, pre-defined responses or financial recommendations.

emtech_SCI_2013.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_SCI_2013.text: 3. AI machines are more intelligent than human beings. (2013)
emtech_SCI_2013.explanation: Current Artificial Intelligence operates as Artificial Narrow Intelligence (ANI), meaning it is highly capable in specific, constrained tasks. However, AI lacks the general intelligence, emotional understanding, adaptability, and broad common sense intrinsic to human beings.

emtech_SCI_2013.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_SCI_2013.text: 4. IOT devices have international standard that enables to communicate with each Other. (2013)
emtech_SCI_2013.explanation: One of the most significant ongoing challenges in the Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystem is the fragmentation and lack of a universal international standard for interoperability, which often impedes seamless communication between devices manufactured by different vendors.

emtech_SCI_2013.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_SCI_2013.text: 5. Unlike VR, AR, integrate digital information on the existing environment. (2013)
emtech_SCI_2013.explanation: Augmented Reality (AR) directly overlays digital information and interactive elements onto the user's real-world environment. In contrast, Virtual Reality (VR) isolates the user from the physical world to immerse them in a completely artificial, computer-generated simulation.

emtech_SCI_2013.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_SCI_2013.text: 1. Which of the following statement is not true about the weaknesses of AI? (2013)

options.text: A. AI machines can accomplish every task away from which they are programmed.
B. With the increase of technology mental creativity and dependency of peoples on Devices decreases.
C. AI machines has no emotions and original creativity

emtech_SCI_2013.explanation: AI cannot accomplish tasks outside of what it has been explicitly programmed or trained to do (making statement A false). Furthermore, as technology increases, human dependency on devices tends to increase, not decrease, and over-reliance can stifle mental creativity (making statement B false). Because both A and B are untrue statements about AI weaknesses, option D is the correct choice.

emtech_SCI_2013.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_SCI_2013.text: 2. Which of the following statement is correct? (2013)

options.text: A. Limited memory machines can store past experiences or some data for a Short period of time.
B. Reactive Machines store memories or experiences for future actions.
C. Narrow AI is the most common currently available AI in the world and it can perform tasks beyond its field.

emtech_SCI_2013.explanation: Limited memory AI models (like those used in autonomous vehicles) can temporarily store past experiences and environmental data to inform immediate future decisions. Reactive machines (Option B) have no concept of the past and cannot store memory. Narrow AI (Option C) is explicitly limited to its specific trained domain and cannot perform tasks beyond its field.

emtech_SCI_2013.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_SCI_2013.text: 3. Which of the following is correctly matched? (2013)

options.text: A. What is happening now? -> Notification
B. What do I need to do right know? -> Situational Awareness
C. What do I need to know -> [unclear]

emtech_SCI_2013.explanation: In IoT data analytics, descriptive analytics answers 'What is happening now?' and is matched with Notification/Awareness triggers. 'What do I need to do right now?' aligns with Prescriptive analytics, and 'What do I need to know?' aligns with Situational Awareness.

emtech_SCI_2013.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_SCI_2013.text: 4. Which of the following statement is correct about IOT? (2013)

options.text: A. IoT devices do most of the work with human intervention.
B. There is no international standard of compatibility for IOT devices.
C. As the number of connected devices increases the potential that a hacker could steal confidential information decrease.

emtech_SCI_2013.explanation: A major operational and structural challenge in the current IoT landscape is the absence of unified international standards for device compatibility, causing integration issues across different manufacturers. IoT largely functions without human intervention, and a larger network of connected devices increases the attack surface for potential hackers.

emtech_SCI_2013.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_SCI_2013.text: 5. Which of the following is the most important features of IOT? (2013)
emtech_SCI_2013.explanation: The core foundational features of IoT include Artificial Intelligence (to process data intelligently), Connectivity (to network devices), Sensors (to capture real-world data), Active Engagement (interacting continuously with users and environments), and the use of small devices. Therefore, all listed options are correct.

emtech_SCI_2013.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_SCI_2013.text: 6. Which of the following layers of IOT is responsible to identify any phenomena in the devices' peripheral and obtain data from the real world. (2013)
emtech_SCI_2013.explanation: The Sensing Layer is the physical layer of the IoT architecture containing sensors and actuators. Its fundamental role is to interface with the physical environment, identify changes or phenomena, and gather raw data for the system to process.

emtech_SCI_2013.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_SCI_2013.text: 7. Which of the following statement is correct about AR, VR and MR? (2013)

options.text: A. In MR the synthetic content and the real-world content are able to react Each other in real-time.
B. VR is a live view of a physical real-world environment
C. AR is a computer-simulated reality.

emtech_SCI_2013.explanation: Mixed Reality (MR) merges real and virtual worlds to produce new environments where physical and digital objects co-exist and interact in real-time. Option B incorrectly describes AR rather than VR, and Option C incorrectly describes VR rather than AR.

emtech_SCI_2013.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_SCI_2013.text: 8. Which of the following is not true about the limitations of Artificial Intelligence? (2013)

options.text: A. Can't think out of the box

emtech_SCI_2013.explanation: AI systems inherently lack the ability to experience feelings or emotions, possess no original human-level creativity, and cannot think 'out of the box' outside their programmed parameters. Since all the provided statements accurately describe real limitations of AI, 'None' of them are untrue.

emtech_SCI_2013.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_SCI_2013.text: 9. Which of the following is influencers of Artificial Intelligence? (2013)
emtech_SCI_2013.explanation: The modern acceleration of Artificial Intelligence has been made possible by a convergence of technological advancements: the availability of massive datasets (Big Data), advanced analytical techniques (Data Science), distributed scalable infrastructure (Cloud Computing), and vast improvements in hardware capabilities (Computer processing power).

emtech_SCI_2013.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_SCI_2013.text: 10. _____ is a machine that has a capability of reasoning, learning and problem solving. (2013)
emtech_SCI_2013.explanation: Artificial Intelligence (AI) refers precisely to machines or software that have been designed to emulate human cognitive functions, specifically encompassing the capabilities to learn from data, reason through logic, and solve complex problems autonomously.

emtech_SCI_2013.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_SCI_2013.text: 1. AI machines are highly Reliable. What does it mean Explain Briefly? (2pts) (2013)
emtech_SCI_2013.answer: Reliability in AI means that the machine can perform a specific task with a consistently high degree of accuracy over extended periods. Unlike humans, AI does not suffer from physical fatigue, distraction, or emotional variance, allowing it to execute repetitive or precision-dependent operations dependably and with fewer errors.
emtech_SCI_2013.explanation: In computing, reliability is a measure of consistent, accurate performance. AI's core advantage in reliability comes from its programmatic execution—once a model is trained to a high accuracy threshold, it will continually apply the exact same logic matrix to incoming data without the degradation in focus that affects human workers.

emtech_SCI_2013.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_SCI_2013.text: 2. What is the difference between Security and Privacy Explain Briefly? (2pts) (2013)
emtech_SCI_2013.answer: Security focuses on the technical and systemic defenses used to protect data and networks from unauthorized access, cyberattacks, or data breaches (e.g., encryption, firewalls). Privacy, on the other hand, deals with user rights and data governance, specifically dictating how personal information is legally collected, used, shared, and controlled with the individual's consent.
emtech_SCI_2013.explanation: Security is fundamentally about protection against malicious threats and ensuring data integrity and confidentiality. Privacy is fundamentally about authorization and compliance, ensuring that even legitimate organizations handle user data ethically and transparently.

emtech_MoSHE_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_MoSHE_2021.university: Ministry of Science and Higher Education
emtech_MoSHE_2021.text: 1. What is the role of data for emerging technologies? (2021)

options.text: A. Determines the future of science and technology
B. Reshaping the world and introducing a paradigm shift
C. Defines the future of economy

emtech_MoSHE_2021.explanation: Data is the fundamental asset driving emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, big data analytics, and the Internet of Things. It directly determines technological advancements, drives transformative paradigm shifts across industries, and forms the cornerstone of modern digital economies.

emtech_MoSHE_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_MoSHE_2021.university: Ministry of Science and Higher Education
emtech_MoSHE_2021.text: 2. Which industrial revolution can be called technological revolution? (2021)
emtech_MoSHE_2021.explanation: The Second Industrial Revolution (roughly 1870 to 1914) is formally termed the Technological Revolution. It was characterized by the introduction of electrical power grids, telephone and telegraph networks, petroleum exploitation, and mass production assembly lines.

emtech_MoSHE_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_MoSHE_2021.university: Ministry of Science and Higher Education
emtech_MoSHE_2021.text: 3. Which Emerging Technologies enabling devices that can store information (2021)
emtech_MoSHE_2021.explanation: Memory devices (such as semiconductor RAM, flash memory, and non-volatile solid-state drives) are specifically designed to store digital information and programs. Microprocessors execute operations, logic devices implement specific circuit logic, and networks transfer data between devices.

emtech_MoSHE_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_MoSHE_2021.university: Ministry of Science and Higher Education
emtech_MoSHE_2021.text: 4. One of the following can't be considered as emerging technologies (2021)
emtech_MoSHE_2021.explanation: Database Management Systems (DBMS) are mature, traditional relational software technologies established decades ago. In contrast, blockchain, big data, and digital twins are disruptive Fourth Industrial Revolution technologies classified as emerging technologies.

emtech_MoSHE_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_MoSHE_2021.university: Ministry of Science and Higher Education
emtech_MoSHE_2021.text: 5. Which of the following is regarded as smart revolution? (2021)
emtech_MoSHE_2021.explanation: The Fourth Industrial Revolution is commonly referred to as the Smart Revolution or Knowledge Revolution because it converges cyber-physical systems, autonomous intelligence, and interconnected smart environments to transform knowledge generation and decision-making.

emtech_MoSHE_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_MoSHE_2021.university: Ministry of Science and Higher Education
emtech_MoSHE_2021.text: 6. Which of the following factor is not considered as a driver of information revolution? (2021)

options.text: A. The growth of information-based occupation
C. The widespread of cheap personal computers
D. The advent of the Internet

emtech_MoSHE_2021.explanation: The Information Revolution (Third Industrial Revolution) was driven by personal computers, telecommunications, the Internet, and information services. Artificial intelligence is a key driver of the Fourth Industrial Revolution rather than the initial Information Revolution.

emtech_MoSHE_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_MoSHE_2021.university: Ministry of Science and Higher Education
emtech_MoSHE_2021.text: 7. The research and development activities in IoT and AI can be examples of _____ industry (2021)
emtech_MoSHE_2021.explanation: The quaternary sector of the economy focuses on knowledge-based, intellectual activities including scientific research, information technology development, data analytics, and engineering in AI and IoT.

emtech_MoSHE_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_MoSHE_2021.university: Ministry of Science and Higher Education
emtech_MoSHE_2021.text: 8. What started the first Industrial Revolution? (2021)

options.text: A. When agricultural societies became more industrialized and urban.
B. Transition to new manufacturing processes going from hand production methods to machines
C. The increasing use of steam power

emtech_MoSHE_2021.explanation: The First Industrial Revolution was initiated by the shift from agrarian societies to mechanized, urban manufacturing, the adoption of machinery over manual craftsmanship, and the utilization of steam and water power.

emtech_MoSHE_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_MoSHE_2021.university: Ministry of Science and Higher Education
emtech_MoSHE_2021.text: 9. The Bidirectional information flow between a human brain and a machine is referred to as (2021)
emtech_MoSHE_2021.explanation: A Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) enables a direct, bidirectional communication link between the brain's neural activity and an external computational or mechanical system.

emtech_MoSHE_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_MoSHE_2021.university: Ministry of Science and Higher Education
emtech_MoSHE_2021.text: 10. One of the following is not the use of the programmable logic devices? (2021)
emtech_MoSHE_2021.explanation: Programmable Logic Devices (such as FPGAs and CPLDs) are integrated circuits configured to implement custom digital logic, signal processing algorithms, and data communication protocols; they are not used as visual display hardware.

emtech_MoSHE_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_MoSHE_2021.university: Ministry of Science and Higher Education
emtech_MoSHE_2021.text: 11. It is a sequence of activities involved in data transformation from its row form to information (2021)
emtech_MoSHE_2021.explanation: Data processing is the organized series of actions (such as validation, sorting, filtering, and aggregation) that converts unorganized raw data into structured, meaningful information.

emtech_MoSHE_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_MoSHE_2021.university: Ministry of Science and Higher Education
emtech_MoSHE_2021.text: 12. Which of the following statement is not correct? (2021)

options.text: A. Unstructured data are straightforward for analysis.
B. Big data acquisition require flexible and dynamic data structures.
C. Semi-structured data contains tags and markers.
D. Data type describe how we intend to use the data in the program.

emtech_MoSHE_2021.explanation: Unstructured data (like video, audio, and natural language text) lacks a predefined data model or organizational schema, making it complex, computationally demanding, and not straightforward to analyze compared to structured data.

emtech_MoSHE_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_MoSHE_2021.university: Ministry of Science and Higher Education
emtech_MoSHE_2021.text: 13. What are the different activities of Big-data life cycle? (2021)

options.text: A. Ingesting data, persisting data, computing and analyzing data, and visualizing results.
B. Acquisition, analysis, curation, storage, and usage.

emtech_MoSHE_2021.explanation: The Big Data life cycle is defined by four core sequential phases: Ingesting data (data collection/import), Persisting data (storage in scalable data stores), Computing and analyzing data (processing and modeling), and Visualizing results (reporting and dashboarding).

emtech_MoSHE_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_MoSHE_2021.university: Ministry of Science and Higher Education
emtech_MoSHE_2021.text: 14. Big Data is characterized by: (2021)
emtech_MoSHE_2021.explanation: Big Data is classically defined by the 3 Vs: Volume (the enormous scale of data), Velocity (the speed of data creation and stream processing), and Variety (the multiplicity of data types: structured, semi-structured, and unstructured).

emtech_MoSHE_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_MoSHE_2021.university: Ministry of Science and Higher Education
emtech_MoSHE_2021.text: 15. Which of the following type of data is currently the most voluminous (largest) of the global data stock? (2021)

options.text: D. Can't be determined for sure

emtech_MoSHE_2021.explanation: Unstructured data—encompassing multimedia files, social media streams, audio, emails, and web content—constitutes approximately 80% to 90% of the world's total digital data volume.

emtech_MoSHE_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_MoSHE_2021.university: Ministry of Science and Higher Education
emtech_MoSHE_2021.text: 16. Which of the following is wrong about data type? (2021)

options.text: A. A data type is an attribute of data in integers, Booleans, and floating-point number.
B. A data type is about the structure of data such as structured, unstructured, and semi-structured.
C. A data type is the structure of the data for a computer programming.
D. A data type is data about data in metadata.

emtech_MoSHE_2021.explanation: Metadata is defined as 'data about data', which describes context and properties of data rather than acting as a programming or computational data type.

emtech_MoSHE_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_MoSHE_2021.university: Ministry of Science and Higher Education
emtech_MoSHE_2021.text: 17. What is the purpose of data science? (2021)

options.text: A. Extract knowledge and insight by finding patterns with data
B. Explore, sort and analyze mega-data from various sources
C. Transform business data into assets that help organizations improve revenue and reduce costs

emtech_MoSHE_2021.explanation: Data science is an interdisciplinary field aimed at discovering hidden patterns, analyzing massive datasets, and converting analytical insights into actionable business and scientific strategies.

emtech_MoSHE_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_MoSHE_2021.university: Ministry of Science and Higher Education
emtech_MoSHE_2021.text: 18. With respect to "computing and analyzing Big data", one of the following tool is different (2021)
emtech_MoSHE_2021.explanation: Apache Hadoop MapReduce is a disk-based, offline batch-processing system, whereas Apache Storm, Apache Flink, and Apache Spark are modern in-memory or real-time streaming engines designed for continuous low-latency computation.

emtech_MoSHE_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_MoSHE_2021.university: Ministry of Science and Higher Education
emtech_MoSHE_2021.text: 19. Which one of the following is not true? (2021)

options.text: A. Data is a raw facts and figures
B. Information is a processed data
C. Data science is simply analyzing data
D. Meta data is data about data

emtech_MoSHE_2021.explanation: Data science is not merely data analysis; it encompasses domain modeling, data engineering, data cleaning, statistical learning, algorithmic design, and actionable intelligence deployment.

emtech_MoSHE_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_MoSHE_2021.university: Ministry of Science and Higher Education
emtech_MoSHE_2021.text: 20. A representation of facts, concepts, or instructions in a formalized manner, which should processing by humans or electronic machine (2021)
emtech_MoSHE_2021.explanation: Data is standardly defined in computing as a formalized representation of facts, numbers, or concepts suitable for communication, interpretation, or processing by humans or automated systems.

emtech_MoSHE_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_MoSHE_2021.university: Ministry of Science and Higher Education
emtech_MoSHE_2021.text: 21. _____ is a branch of computer science by which we can create intelligence machines that can behave like a human. (2021)
emtech_MoSHE_2021.explanation: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is the branch of computer science focused on designing systems and algorithms capable of mimicking human cognitive functions such as learning, reasoning, perception, and problem-solving.

emtech_MoSHE_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_MoSHE_2021.university: Ministry of Science and Higher Education
emtech_MoSHE_2021.text: 22. All are correct about artificial intelligence, except_____ (2021)
emtech_MoSHE_2021.explanation: Artificial intelligence systems are mathematical models and computational engines that lack consciousness, sentience, feelings, and emotions.

emtech_MoSHE_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_MoSHE_2021.university: Ministry of Science and Higher Education
emtech_MoSHE_2021.text: 23. [unclear] of the following are teachers today using to enhance learning? (2021)

options.text: D. increasing the number of field trips giving more

emtech_MoSHE_2021.explanation: Modern instructional technology incorporates Web 3.0 semantic and decentralized tools to facilitate personalized, interactive, and intelligent learning environments for students.

emtech_MoSHE_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_MoSHE_2021.university: Ministry of Science and Higher Education
emtech_MoSHE_2021.text: 24. _____ is anything that can perceive its environment through sensory and acts upon environment through effectors (2021)
emtech_MoSHE_2021.explanation: In AI terminology, an Agent is any entity that perceives its environment through sensors and directs its activity upon that environment using effectors/actuators.

emtech_MoSHE_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_MoSHE_2021.university: Ministry of Science and Higher Education
emtech_MoSHE_2021.text: 25. Machine perception is achieved by_____ (2021)
emtech_MoSHE_2021.explanation: Machine perception is the process by which a computer system interprets sensory data from the physical world, which is captured via hardware sensors such as cameras, microphones, and LiDAR.

emtech_MoSHE_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_MoSHE_2021.university: Ministry of Science and Higher Education
emtech_MoSHE_2021.text: 26. An expert system differs from a database program in that only an expert system (2021)

options.text: C. Features the retrieval of stored information
D. Expects users to draw their own conclusions

emtech_MoSHE_2021.explanation: Unlike standard database programs that simply store and retrieve declarative facts, expert systems use procedural and heuristic knowledge in an inference engine to reason and solve complex problems.

emtech_MoSHE_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_MoSHE_2021.university: Ministry of Science and Higher Education
emtech_MoSHE_2021.text: 27. Which of the following is not an advantage of Artificial Intelligence (2021)

options.text: A. High Accuracy with fewer errors
C. Useful as a public utility

emtech_MoSHE_2021.explanation: Increased human dependency on automated machines is a vulnerability and disadvantage of AI systems, whereas high accuracy, high reliability, and operational speed are advantages.

emtech_MoSHE_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_MoSHE_2021.university: Ministry of Science and Higher Education
emtech_MoSHE_2021.text: 28. One of the following is not the application of AI. (2021)
emtech_MoSHE_2021.explanation: Conversational chatbots, recommendation systems, and automated travel booking systems are all direct real-world applications of AI; therefore, 'None' is the correct selection.

emtech_MoSHE_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_MoSHE_2021.university: Ministry of Science and Higher Education
emtech_MoSHE_2021.text: 29. What type of Artificial Intelligence which is an ability of machine to learn without being explicitly programmed? (2021)
emtech_MoSHE_2021.explanation: Machine Learning is specifically defined as the subfield of AI that enables systems to automatically learn from data and improve their performance on tasks without being explicitly programmed.

emtech_MoSHE_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_MoSHE_2021.university: Ministry of Science and Higher Education
emtech_MoSHE_2021.text: 30. Artificial Intelligence (AI) devices such as Siri (Apple) Alexa (Amazon) Cortana (Microsoft), etc. can be operated by (2021)
emtech_MoSHE_2021.explanation: Virtual voice assistants such as Siri, Alexa, and Cortana primarily rely on natural language processing and voice recognition technologies to understand and respond to spoken user commands.

emtech_MoSHE_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_MoSHE_2021.university: Ministry of Science and Higher Education
emtech_MoSHE_2021.text: 31. _____ is the networking of smart objects that communicate intelligently in the presence of internet protocol. (2021)
emtech_MoSHE_2021.explanation: The Internet of Things (IoT) is defined as the interconnected network of physical smart devices containing embedded sensors, software, and network connectivity that communicate over IP networks.

emtech_MoSHE_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_MoSHE_2021.university: Ministry of Science and Higher Education
emtech_MoSHE_2021.text: 32. One of the following IoTchallenges that describe the connected devices communicating over networks exposes users to various kinds of security attack. (2021)
emtech_MoSHE_2021.explanation: The Security challenge in IoT refers to the vulnerabilities of large numbers of interconnected endpoints to unauthorized access, cyberattacks, and malware exploitation.

emtech_MoSHE_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_MoSHE_2021.university: Ministry of Science and Higher Education
emtech_MoSHE_2021.text: 33. Which of the following is not IoT features? (2021)
emtech_MoSHE_2021.explanation: IoT architectures emphasize autonomous machine-to-machine (M2M) communication and automated sensing, aiming to minimize or eliminate direct human intervention.

emtech_MoSHE_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_MoSHE_2021.university: Ministry of Science and Higher Education
emtech_MoSHE_2021.text: 34. One of the following is disadvantage of IoTsystem? (2021)
emtech_MoSHE_2021.explanation: Device interoperability issues arise from the lack of universal standards among different manufacturers, creating compatibility challenges across diverse IoT hardware and software systems.

emtech_MoSHE_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_MoSHE_2021.university: Ministry of Science and Higher Education
emtech_MoSHE_2021.text: 35. IoT devices in the form of wearable's like Fitbit, smart eyeglass and health monitors makes life much easier. This is an application of IoT in (2021)
emtech_MoSHE_2021.explanation: Wearable electronic devices such as smart fitness bands, health monitors, and smart glasses are developed directly for individual lifestyle and consumer applications.

emtech_MoSHE_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_MoSHE_2021.university: Ministry of Science and Higher Education
emtech_MoSHE_2021.text: 36. Which layer of the IoT architecture is responsible to take measurements such as temperature, air quality, speed, humidity, pressure, flow, movement and electricity etc.? (2021)
emtech_MoSHE_2021.explanation: The Sensing (or Perception) Layer is the physical baseline layer of IoT architecture responsible for detecting physical phenomena and collecting environmental measurements through various sensors and actuators.

emtech_MoSHE_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_MoSHE_2021.university: Ministry of Science and Higher Education
emtech_MoSHE_2021.text: 43. [truncated] (2021)
emtech_MoSHE_2021.explanation: Virtual Reality is an immersive, computer-generated visual and auditory simulation that completely replaces the user's perception of the physical environment.

emtech_MoSHE_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_MoSHE_2021.university: Ministry of Science and Higher Education
emtech_MoSHE_2021.text: 44. Suppose you have a cell-phone app that is designed in such a way that when camera is focused on a historical monument, it displays a digital information about the monument. Which technology do you think is this app using? (2021)
emtech_MoSHE_2021.explanation: Augmented Reality (AR) enhances the real-world view by superimposing contextual digital information, labels, or 3D models onto live physical objects through a camera display.

emtech_MoSHE_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_MoSHE_2021.university: Ministry of Science and Higher Education
emtech_MoSHE_2021.text: 45. Which one of the following is not true? (2021)

options.text: B. Augmented Reality uses the existing environment and overlays new information on top of it.
C. Augmented Reality is also called a computer-simulated Reality

emtech_MoSHE_2021.explanation: Virtual Reality, not Augmented Reality, is termed computer-simulated reality because it creates a fully synthetic artificial environment. AR merely augments the existing physical environment with digital elements.

emtech_MoSHE_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_MoSHE_2021.university: Ministry of Science and Higher Education
emtech_MoSHE_2021.text: 46. _____ in Augmented reality architecture makes the user interface available in browser? (2021)
emtech_MoSHE_2021.explanation: In AR system architecture, the Client tier runs on the user's local device/browser, rendering the visual interface and processing local user interactions and sensory streams.

emtech_MoSHE_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_MoSHE_2021.university: Ministry of Science and Higher Education
emtech_MoSHE_2021.text: 47. One of the following statements is not correct about virtual reality (2021)

options.text: A. A new world is created out of the mixt of virtual and physical objects
B. Uses head-mounted devices to display a digital world of imagery and sound
C. Completely separates the user from its real environment

emtech_MoSHE_2021.explanation: Mixing real and virtual objects describes Mixed Reality (MR) or Augmented Reality (AR). Virtual Reality (VR) replaces the physical environment entirely with an exclusively computer-generated synthetic world.

emtech_MoSHE_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_MoSHE_2021.university: Ministry of Science and Higher Education
emtech_MoSHE_2021.text: 48. Which of the following is not immersive technologies? (2021)
emtech_MoSHE_2021.explanation: A natural real environment is the physical world and not a digital immersive technology. Immersive technologies encompass virtual reality, augmented reality, and mixed reality.

emtech_MoSHE_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_MoSHE_2021.university: Ministry of Science and Higher Education
emtech_MoSHE_2021.text: 49. One of the following is true about Virtual reality? (2021)

options.text: A. Google class is an example of virtual reality device
B. Smart phone are used in virtual reality
C. It requires devices like Head mounted display
D. Users can interact with real environment objects

emtech_MoSHE_2021.explanation: Virtual Reality relies on Head-Mounted Displays (HMDs) to enclose the user's visual field and deliver stereoscopic views that fully immerse the user in the virtual environment.

emtech_MoSHE_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_MoSHE_2021.university: Ministry of Science and Higher Education
emtech_MoSHE_2021.text: 50. A type of VR environment in which subjects are visually isolated from the real environment (2021)
emtech_MoSHE_2021.explanation: Fully immersive Virtual Reality completely isolates the user visually and auditorily from the physical environment using headsets, providing a full sense of psychological and physical presence in the simulated world.

emtech_AASTU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AASTU_2021.text: 1. What is Artificial Intelligence? (2021)

options.text: A. A field that aims to make humans more intelligent
B. A field that aims to improve the security
C. A field that aims to develop intelligent machines
D. A field that aims to mine the data

emtech_AASTU_2021.explanation: Artificial Intelligence is broadly defined as the branch of computer science dedicated to developing intelligent machines capable of performing tasks that typically require human intelligence. While it can interact with security or data mining, its fundamental goal is the creation of intelligent systems.

emtech_AASTU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AASTU_2021.text: 2. Which of the following is not a fundamental component of an IoT system? (2021)
emtech_AASTU_2021.explanation: A complete IoT architecture essentially consists of four main components: sensors/devices, connectivity, data processing, and a user interface. A transformer is an electrical device used to step up or step down voltage and is not a fundamental component of an IoT system.

emtech_AASTU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AASTU_2021.text: 3. ________ is the system of rules that govern the ordering of values? (2021)
emtech_AASTU_2021.explanation: Ethics is formally defined as the system of moral principles and rules that govern human behavior and the ordering of values. It provides the framework for determining what is considered right or wrong in a given context.

emtech_AASTU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AASTU_2021.text: 4. Which one of the following is not the disadvantage of AI? (2021)

options.text: A. Useful as a public utility
C. Can't think out of the box

emtech_AASTU_2021.explanation: Being useful as a public utility is a major advantage of AI, as it enables the optimization of large-scale resources like energy and transportation. High costs, lack of creativity (thinking out of the box), lack of emotions, and increased dependency are all recognized disadvantages.

emtech_AASTU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AASTU_2021.text: 5. ________ is an advanced type of object detection which identifies a specific individual? (2021)
emtech_AASTU_2021.explanation: Facial recognition is an advanced computer vision technology that goes beyond basic object detection to uniquely identify or verify a specific human individual based on their facial features.

emtech_AASTU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AASTU_2021.text: 6. ________ is the merging of real and virtual worlds to produce new environments and visualizations where physical and digital objects co-exist and interact in real-time? (2021)
emtech_AASTU_2021.explanation: Mixed Reality (MR) is defined as the merging of the real and virtual worlds where physical and digital objects can coexist and interact in real-time. This distinguishes it from Augmented Reality (AR), which merely overlays digital content, and Virtual Reality (VR), which is fully immersive.

emtech_AASTU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AASTU_2021.text: 13. What risks and challenges should be considered in the internet of things? (2021)
emtech_AASTU_2021.explanation: The deployment of IoT systems introduces multiple challenges. These include severe privacy and security vulnerabilities, massive energy consumption from millions of devices, and heavy network congestion due to continuous data transmission. Therefore, all these factors must be considered.

emtech_AASTU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AASTU_2021.text: 14. How many main components IoT mainly consists of? (2021)
emtech_AASTU_2021.explanation: An IoT system is fundamentally composed of four distinct components: sensors/devices (for data collection), connectivity (for data transmission), data processing (for analyzing the data), and a user interface (for user interaction).

emtech_AASTU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AASTU_2021.text: 15. Augmented reality (AR) provides features that are ________? (2021)
emtech_AASTU_2021.explanation: According to the standard definitions of Augmented Reality (such as Azuma's criteria), AR provides features that are inherently visual, interactive in real-time, and spatially registered in 3D to properly align digital overlays with the physical environment.

emtech_AASTU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AASTU_2021.text: 16. AR technology allows students to interact with the physical world by ________? (2021)

options.text: A. Moving around to change perspectives
B. Moving closer/further to change the scale
C. Select virtual objects by pointing to them

emtech_AASTU_2021.explanation: AR technology maps digital objects onto the real world, allowing dynamic spatial interaction. Users can physically move around to view digital elements from different perspectives, step closer or further to adjust the scale, and interactively point at or select objects.

emtech_AASTU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AASTU_2021.text: 17. Which of the following does not come under the three pillars of digital privacy? (2021)
emtech_AASTU_2021.explanation: The three foundational pillars of digital privacy recognized in information security are Information privacy (data protection), Individual privacy (personal bodily/spatial rights), and Communication privacy (secure messaging). Family privacy is not a standard pillar in this context.

emtech_AASTU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AASTU_2021.text: 18. In Levels of AI, the stage 3 is ________? (2021)
emtech_AASTU_2021.explanation: In the standard categorization of AI maturity stages, Stage 1 represents Rule-Based Systems, Stage 2 is Context Awareness, and Stage 3 is Domain-Specific Expertise, where systems achieve high proficiency in dedicated fields (e.g., medical diagnosis or chess).

emtech_AASTU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AASTU_2021.text: 19. Which is Not one of the challenges of the Internet of Things? (2021)
emtech_AASTU_2021.explanation: Technology Optimization is a primary advantage and goal of implementing IoT, as it leads to better efficiency and automation. Conversely, Privacy, Security, and Flexibility (integration difficulties) are major challenges.

emtech_AASTU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AASTU_2021.text: 20. Of the following systems, which one can be taken as an example/definition of a "General AI"? (2021)

options.text: A. Systems at which machines could exceed human intelligence
B. Systems that perform any intellectual task with efficiency like a human
C. Systems that perform a dedicated task with intelligence

emtech_AASTU_2021.explanation: Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) refers to systems that possess cognitive abilities equivalent to a human, allowing them to perform any intellectual task a human can. Systems that perform a dedicated task are Narrow AI, and systems that exceed human intelligence are Super AI.

emtech_AASTU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AASTU_2021.text: 21. Based on the state-of-the-art AI maturity level, which one of the following can be performed using any AI algorithm EXCEPT: (2021)

options.text: A. Perceive things the way humans do
C. Predict the future based on the current trend
D. Conscious of the algorithm itself

emtech_AASTU_2021.explanation: Current state-of-the-art AI operates strictly within the realm of Narrow AI. While these systems can perceive environments (via sensors/vision), automate tasks, and run predictive analytics, they completely lack self-awareness and consciousness.

emtech_AASTU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AASTU_2021.text: 22. Which one of the following is not one of the benefits we can get by merely using IoT? (2021)
emtech_AASTU_2021.explanation: Merely using IoT hardware facilitates enhanced data collection, improved engagement, and reduced waste. However, the intelligent analysis of this massive data requires the integration of Artificial Intelligence or Big Data analytics, rather than being an inherent feature of just the IoT sensors themselves.

emtech_AASTU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AASTU_2021.text: 23. Which one of the following is one of the challenges of using IoT EXCEPT? (2021)

options.text: A. Users can be exposed to hackers
B. Individual private data can easily become in the hands of intruders
C. May fail to comply with regulations
D. Difficult to integrate with other existing or the would-be existing systems

emtech_AASTU_2021.explanation: All the listed options represent valid challenges of using IoT: exposure to hackers (Security), data intrusion (Privacy), regulatory failures (Compliance), and integration difficulties (Flexibility/Complexity). Since there are no exceptions among A, B, C, and D, 'None' is the correct answer.

emtech_AASTU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AASTU_2021.text: 24. A real person (one of us) interacting (playing or fighting against) with a computer generate humanoid is an example of ________? (2021)
emtech_AASTU_2021.explanation: Mixed Reality (MR) explicitly allows real-world physical elements (like a human user) and digital elements (like a computer-generated humanoid) to co-exist and actively interact in real-time. This dynamic interplay goes beyond the simple overlays of AR.

emtech_AASTU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AASTU_2021.text: 25. When we breach the digital privacy that the messages and communications will only be accessible to the sender's original intended recipient, specifically we are breaching: (2021)
emtech_AASTU_2021.explanation: Communication privacy is the specific domain of digital privacy that ensures conversations, emails, and messages remain secure and accessible only to the sender and the explicitly intended recipients without interception.

emtech_AASTU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AASTU_2021.text: 26. Which of the following does not come under the three pillars of digital privacy? (2021)
emtech_AASTU_2021.explanation: The three widely recognized pillars of digital privacy are Information privacy, Individual privacy, and Communication privacy. Family privacy is a distinct social concept and not one of the technical digital privacy pillars.

emtech_AASTU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AASTU_2021.text: 27. ________ technology makes users feel as if they truly are in a virtual environment? (2021)
emtech_AASTU_2021.explanation: Virtual Reality (VR) uses entirely computer-generated environments and fully immerses the user, often through a headset, replacing their real-world vision so they feel truly present within the simulation.

emtech_AASTU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AASTU_2021.text: 28. Which one of the following is incorrect about reactive machines? (2021)

options.text: A. Reactive machines can store past experiences or some data for a short period.
B. Reactive machines are the most basic types of Artificial Intelligence
C. IBM's Deep Blue system is an example of reactive machines
D. They only focus on current scenarios and react to them as per possible best action.

emtech_AASTU_2021.explanation: Reactive machines are the most basic type of AI and have absolutely no concept of the past; they cannot store past experiences or data to inform future actions. AI that stores temporary past data is known as Limited Memory AI.

emtech_AASTU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AASTU_2021.text: 29. Which of the following is not an advantage of IoT? (2021)
emtech_AASTU_2021.explanation: Security is widely recognized as one of the largest challenges and disadvantages of IoT systems due to the vast attack surface created by millions of connected devices. The other options are well-established advantages.

emtech_AASTU_2021.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_AASTU_2021.text: 30. ________ of an IoT system is the capability to easily integrate with another system (2021)
emtech_AASTU_2021.explanation: Flexibility in the context of IoT refers to the system's interoperability and capability to seamlessly integrate with other systems and protocols without being locked into a single vendor's rigid ecosystem.

emtech_EU_2022.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_EU_2022.text: 1. What is the role of data for emerging technologies? (2022)

options.text: A. Determines the future of science and technology
B. Reshaping the world and introducing a paradigm shift
C. Defines the future of economy

emtech_EU_2022.explanation: Data serves as the foundational fuel for modern emerging technologies. It drives advancements in science and engineering, transforms global economic models, and reshapes societal structures through automated and intelligent systems.

emtech_EU_2022.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_EU_2022.text: 2. Which industrial revolution can be called technological revolution? (2022)
emtech_EU_2022.explanation: The Second Industrial Revolution (roughly 1870–1914) is historically known as the Technological Revolution. It was characterized by the widespread adoption of pre-existing technological systems such as electrical power grids, the internal combustion engine, and telecommunications.

emtech_EU_2022.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_EU_2022.text: 3. Which emerging technology enabling devices that can store information (2022)
emtech_EU_2022.explanation: Memory devices (such as RAM, ROM, and flash storage) are the core hardware components specifically engineered to store digital information. Microprocessors and logic devices process data, while networks provide communication channels.

emtech_EU_2022.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_EU_2022.text: 4. One of the following can't be considered as emerging technologies. (2022)
emtech_EU_2022.explanation: A Database Management System (DBMS) is a traditional, mature computing technology established in the 1960s and 1970s. In contrast, blockchain, big data analytics, and digital twins are modern emerging technologies defining the Fourth Industrial Revolution.

emtech_EU_2022.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_EU_2022.text: 5. Which of the following is regarded as smart revolution? (2022)
emtech_EU_2022.explanation: The Knowledge Revolution (associated with the Fourth Industrial Revolution) is regarded as the Smart Revolution because it leverages artificial intelligence, cognitive systems, and smart automation to autonomously generate and apply knowledge.

emtech_EU_2022.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_EU_2022.text: 6. Which of the following factor is not considered as a driver of information revolution? (2022)

options.text: A. The growth of information-based occupation
C. The widespread of cheap personal computers
D. The advent of the Internet

emtech_EU_2022.explanation: The Information Revolution (Third Industrial Revolution) was primarily driven by personal computing, the Internet, and the expansion of information-based occupations. Artificial intelligence is the key driver of the Fourth Industrial Revolution rather than the initial Information Revolution.

emtech_EU_2022.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_EU_2022.text: 7. The research and development activities in IoT and AI can be examples of _____ industry (2022)
emtech_EU_2022.explanation: The Quaternary sector of industry is knowledge-based and encompasses research and development (R&D), information technology, and scientific innovation such as AI and IoT research.

emtech_EU_2022.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_EU_2022.text: 8. What started the first Industrial Revolution? (2022)

options.text: A. When agricultural societies became more industrialized and urban.
B. Transition to new manufacturing processes going from hand production methods to machines
C. The increasing use of steam power

emtech_EU_2022.explanation: The First Industrial Revolution was initiated by the widespread shift from agrarian societies to mechanized, urban manufacturing, powered by the invention and adoption of steam engines and machine tools.

emtech_EU_2022.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_EU_2022.text: 9. The Bidirectional information flow between a human brain and a machine is referred to as (2022)
emtech_EU_2022.explanation: A Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) enables a direct, bidirectional pathway of communication between the neural activity of a biological brain and an external computer or machine.

emtech_EU_2022.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_EU_2022.text: 10. One of the following is not the use of the programmable logic devices? (2022)
emtech_EU_2022.explanation: Programmable Logic Devices (PLDs) are semiconductor devices configured to implement custom digital hardware logic, signal processing, and data communication functions. They do not function as display units.

emtech_EU_2022.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_EU_2022.text: 11. It is a sequence of activities involved in data transformation from its row form to information (2022)
emtech_EU_2022.explanation: Data processing is the comprehensive sequence of operations performed on raw data to transform, structure, and convert it into meaningful information.

emtech_EU_2022.subject: Emerging Technologies
emtech_EU_2022.text: 12. Which of the following statement is not correct? (2022)
